title: Row sums of Catalan's triangle: Σₖ T(n,k) = C(2n+1, n)

problemStatement.plain: Catalan's triangle is a two-parameter array of ballot numbers T(n,k), each counting monotone lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,k) that never rise above the main diagonal; its diagonal entries T(n,n) are the Catalan numbers. This problem asks us to sum an entire row: prove that T(n,0) + T(n,1) + ... + T(n,n) collapses to the single central-binomial value C(2n+1, n), aggregating the reflection-principle counts across the row and tying the triangle back to the Catalan/central-binomial family. The task is to formalize this row-sum identity in Lean 4 on top of the parent's already-verified ballotNumber object and its closed form.
whyMatters: Row sums close the loop between the Catalan triangle and the central-binomial sequence that generates it, showing that aggregating reflection-principle counts across a row reproduces C(2n+1, n).
It is the natural next structural fact after the parent established individual entries, their closed form, and the lattice-path recurrence.

Formalizing it exercises finite-sum manipulation of binomial coefficients (telescoping / hockey-stick aggregation), a recurring enumerative pattern with no dedicated Catalan-triangle instance in Mathlib.

open: The closed evaluation of the full row sum Σ_{k=0}^{n} T(n,k) as C(2n+1, n) is not formalized in the gallery or Mathlib.
The bridge relating C(2n+1, n) to the succeeding Catalan number catalan (n+1) (the ballot-aggregation reading) is not yet recorded.
knownResults.goal: Prove in Lean 4 over ℕ the identity ∑ k in Finset.range (n+1), ballotNumber n k = (2*n+1).choose n, reusing the parent's ballotNumber definition and its closed form; a genuine bijective (Finset-of-paths) proof is out of scope.
